Resolves #18899

`VDomUpdate#getMergedChildIds()` adds a merged child's bridge path only when the walk up its `parentId` chain reaches the owner. A child re-parented out of the owner's subtree after it merged used to drag every ancestor up to the root into the owner's flight. The collision filter then dropped the owner's own payload as covered, and the owner never settled: the `vdom update wedged` watchdog class that #18885 measured in a grid.

Evidence: **L1** — the registry and a real flight in the unit tier (`useDomApiRenderer`, no VDom worker), red without the fix.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline jobs ran. Change class: `defect` (`fix`).

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `unit/vdom/ReparentedMergedChild.spec.mjs` › "the bridge stops at the owner, so it holds none of the new parent's ancestors" |
| AC-2 | the same spec › "the owner's next flight settles, even when an ancestor of the new parent covers the owner" |
| AC-3 | both arms first assert the bridge of a child still inside the subtree (`child` + `mid`); the full unit tier is green, the merge specs included |

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #18899 with its registry probe. `dev`'s `VDomUpdate#getMergedChildIds()` (the unguarded `parentId` walk) and `registerMerged()`. `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate()`'s collision filter, which drops a payload that an ancestor's depth covers. The `#12946` wedge class. `grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` re-parenting the editor on every render, which is what made the case ordinary.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Add the bridge only when the walk reaches the owner; otherwise the child goes out as its own disjoint payload. Nothing outside the owner's subtree may join the owner's flight. It must NOT special-case grids or editors, or drop the re-parented child's own update. Test isolation: unit arms at the registry and on the flight, where the owner settles and its in-flight registration clears.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. The walk collects into `bridge` and commits it only when `component?.parentId === ownerId`, which covers all three ways the loop ends: a lookup miss, the root reached, the owner reached. The child stays in the set from `item.children.keys()`, so its payload still goes out.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The defect was reproduced below the grid, at the registry, before the fix was written. The trace (the center body's flight keyed to `neo-viewport-1` alone) is what located it.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (non-blocking; a neighbour, not this diff): `VdomLifecycle#mergeIntoParentUpdate(parentId=this.parentId, distance=1)` walks the same chain by recursion, and its default parameter re-substitutes `this.parentId` whenever an ancestor's `parentId` is `undefined`. I measured a symptom earlier today. `Neo.worker.App.createNeoInstance({ntype: 'grid-container', parentId: undefined, …})` fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, the stack repeating `GridBody.mergeIntoParentUpdate (VdomLifecycle.mjs:806)`. The default-parameter reading is my inference from that stack. The two parent walks are the same shape and share one weakness, an unguarded termination, so worth a ticket beside #18900.
- **Documented search:** I looked for three regressions and found none:
  - a child still inside the subtree losing its bridge: the arm asserts `child` + `mid` first;
  - a distance-1 child changing behaviour: it skips the walk, unchanged;
  - the re-parented child's own update never settling: it stays in the set, and the arm checks the owner's `promiseUpdate()` settles and `isVdomUpdating` clears.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: A merged child can be re-parented while its merge is pending. `grid.Row` does it on every render, and `container.Base#insert` does it for any moved item. So any walk over a merged child's `parentId` chain must survive the chain changing between registration and collection.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: N/A
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: A wedge that shows up in a grid lock change was a three-component registry bug. Reproducing below the component that surfaced it is what kept the fix to three lines.
